topicName: Agile Scrum & Kanban Frameworks for QA
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Agile Scrum and Kanban Frameworks for QA in Manual Testing"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Quality Assurance (QA) plays a pivotal role in Agile environments. Unlike traditional waterfall models where testing happens at the end of the development cycle, Agile integrates testing continuously throughout the software development life cycle (SDLC). This tutorial explores how manual testers fit into the two most popular Agile frameworks: Scrum and Kanban."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"1. Understanding Agile QA Fundamentals"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In Agile, QA is not just a phase; it is a mindset. Manual testers work closely with product owners, developers, and stakeholders to ensure software quality from inception to deployment. The core principles include early testing, frequent feedback loops, and adaptability to change."},{"order":5,"type":"heading","text":"2. Scrum Framework for Manual Testers"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"Scrum is an iterative framework that divides work into fixed-length iterations called Sprints, typically lasting 2 to 4 weeks. Here is how manual testers participate in Scrum ceremonies and workflows."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Sprint Planning and QA Involvement"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"During Sprint Planning, the team selects items from the Product Backlog. Manual testers must review user stories for testability, identify missing requirements, and estimate the effort required for manual testing within the sprint timeframe."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Daily Standups"},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Report testing progress on current user stories."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Highlight blockers such as environment instability or delayed builds."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Coordinate with developers on bug fixes and re-testing priorities."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Sprint Review and Retrospective"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the Sprint Review, the team demonstrates the completed increment. Manual testers validate that user stories meet the Acceptance Criteria (AC). During the Retrospective, the QA engineer contributes ideas to improve testing bottlenecks and process inefficiencies."},{"order":15,"type":"heading","text":"3. Kanban Framework for Manual Testers"},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"Kanban is a visual workflow management method focused on continuous delivery without fixed-length sprints. Work items are represented on a Kanban board, emphasizing flow and limiting Work in Progress (WIP)."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Typical Kanban Board Columns for QA"},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Backlog: Prioritized user stories waiting to be picked up."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In Development: Developers write code and perform unit testing."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ready for QA: Code is deployed to the test environment; manual testing begins."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"In QA / Testing: Manual execution of test cases, exploratory testing, and bug logging."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Blocked: Tickets stuck due to environment issues or unclear requirements."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Done: Features successfully verified and ready for release."},{"order":24,"type":"heading","text":"4. Best Practices for Manual Testers in Agile"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shift Left Testing: Begin writing test scenarios and acceptance criteria as soon as user stories are drafted."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Adopt Behavior-Driven Development (BDD): Collaborate with stakeholders using Given-When-Then syntax to define clear test conditions."},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Perform Exploratory Testing: Dedicate time for unscripted testing to uncover subtle UI and UX defects that scripted tests miss."},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Manage WIP Limits: In Kanban, avoid pulling too many tickets into testing simultaneously to prevent context switching and bottlenecks."},{"order":29,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Whether operating in Scrum sprints or a continuous Kanban flow, manual testers must be adaptable, communicative, and proactive. By integrating closely with the development team and focusing on rapid feedback, QA professionals ensure high-quality software delivery in modern Agile organizations."}]
